source_text_or_hash: Sun Tzu said: The art of war is of vital importance to the State.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: It is a matter of life and death, a road either to safety or to ruin. Hence it is a subject of inquiry which can on no account be neglected.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The art of war, then, is governed by five constant factors, to be taken into account in one’s deliberations, when seeking to determine the conditions obtaining in the field.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: These are:
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The Moral Law;
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Heaven;
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Earth;
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The Commander;
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Method and discipline.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The Moral Law causes the people to be in complete accord with their ruler, so that they will follow him regardless of their lives, undismayed by any danger.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Heaven signifies night and day, cold and heat, times and seasons.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Earth comprises distances, great and small; danger and security; open ground and narrow passes; the chances of life and death.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The Commander stands for the virtues of wisdom, sincerely, benevolence, courage and strictness.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: By method and discipline are to be understood the marshalling of the army in its proper subdivisions, the graduations of rank among the officers, the maintenance of roads by which supplies may reach the army, and the control of military expenditure.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: These five heads should be familiar to every general: he who knows them will be victorious; he who knows them not will fail.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Therefore, in your deliberations, when seeking to determine the military conditions, let them be made the basis of a comparison, in this wise:
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Which of the two sovereigns is imbued with the Moral law?
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Which of the two generals has the most ability?
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: With whom lie the advantages derived from Heaven and Earth?
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: On which side is discipline most rigorously enforced?
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Which army is stronger?
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: On which side are officers and men more highly trained?
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: In which army is there the greater consistency both in reward and punishment?
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: By means of these seven considerations I can forecast victory or defeat.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The general that hearkens to my counsel and acts upon it, will conquer: let such a one be retained in command! The general that hearkens not to my counsel nor acts upon it, will suffer defeat:—let such a one be dismissed!
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: While heading the profit of my counsel, avail yourself also of any helpful circumstances over and beyond the ordinary rules.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: As circumstances are favourable, one should modify one’s plans.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: All warfare is based on deception.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hence, when able to attack, we must seem unable; when using our forces, we must seem inactive; when we are near, we must make the enemy believe we are far away; when far away, we must make him believe we are near.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hold out baits to entice the enemy. Feign disorder, and crush him.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If he is secure at all points, be prepared for him. If he is in superior strength, evade him.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If he is taking his ease, give him no rest. If his forces are united, separate them.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If your opponent is of choleric temper, seek to irritate him. Pretend to be weak, that he may grow arrogant.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Attack him where he is unprepared, appear where you are not expected.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: These military devices, leading to victory, must not be divulged beforehand.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Now the general who wins a battle makes many calculations in his temple where the battle is fought. The general who loses a battle makes a few calculations beforehand. Thus doing many calculations lead to victory, and few calculations to defeat: how much more no calculation at all! It is by attention to this point that I can foresee who is likely to win or lose.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Waging War
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Sun Tzu said: In the operations of war, where there are in the field a thousand swift chariots, as many heavy chariots, and a hundred thousand mail-clad soldiers, with provisions enough to carry them a thousand li, the expenditure at home and at the front, including entertainment of guests, small items such as glue and paint, and sums spent on chariots and armour, will reach the total of a thousand ounces of silver per day. Such is the cost of raising an army of 100,000 men.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When you engage in actual fighting, if victory is long in coming, then men’s weapons will grow dull and their ardour will be damped. If you lay siege to a town, you will exhaust your strength.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Again, if the campaign is protracted, the resources of the State will not be equal to the strain.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When their substance is drained away, the peasantry will be afflicted by heavy exactions.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Now, when your weapons are dulled, your ardour damped, your strength exhausted and your treasure spent, other chieftains will spring up to take advantage of your extremity. Then no man, however wise, will be able to avert the consequences that must ensue.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Thus, though we have heard of stupid haste in war, cleverness has never been seen associated with long delays.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: There is no instance of a country having benefited from prolonged warfare.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: It is only one who is thoroughly acquainted with the evils of war that can thoroughly understand the profitable way of carrying it on.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The skilful soldier does not raise a second levy, nor are his supply-wagons loaded more than twice.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Bring war material with you from home, but forage on the enemy. Thus the army will have enough food for its needs.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Poverty of the State exchequer causes an army to be maintained by contributions from a distance. Contributing to maintaining an army at a distance causes the people to be impoverished.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: On the other hand, the proximity of an army causes prices to go up; and high prices cause the people’s substance to be drained away.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: With this loss of substance and exhaustion of strength, the homes of the people will be stripped bare, and three-tenths of their income will be dissipated; while government expenses for broken chariots, worn-out horses, breast-plates and helmets, bows and arrows, spears and shields, protective mantles, draught-oxen and heavy wagons, will amount to four-tenths of its total revenue.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Now in order to kill the enemy, our men must be roused to anger; that there may be advantages from defeating the enemy, they must have their rewards.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hence a wise general makes a point of foraging on the enemy. One cartload of the enemy’s provisions is equivalent to twenty of one’s own, and likewise a single picul of his provender is equivalent to twenty from one’s own store.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Therefore in chariot fighting, when ten or more chariots have been taken, those should be rewarded who took the first. Our own flags should be substituted for those of the enemy, and the chariots mingled and used in conjunction with ours. The captured soldiers should be kindly treated and kept.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Thus it may be known that the leader of armies is the arbiter of the people’s fate, the man on whom it depends whether the nation shall be in peace or in peril.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: This is called, using the conquered foe to augment one’s own strength.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: In war, then, let your great object be victory, not lengthy campaigns.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Attack by Stratagem
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Sun Tzu said: In the practical art of war, the best thing of all is to take the enemy’s country whole and intact; to shatter and destroy it is not so good. So, too, it is better to recapture an entire army than to destroy it, to capture a regiment, a detachment or a company entirely rather than to destroy them.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hence to fight and conquer in all your battles is not supreme excellence; supreme excellence consists in breaking the enemy’s resistance without fighting.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Thus the highest form of generalship is to block the enemy’s plans; the next best is to prevent the junction of the enemy’s forces; the next in order is to attack the enemy’s army in the field; and the worst policy of all is to besiege walled cities.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The rule is, not to besiege walled cities if it can possibly be avoided. The preparation of mantlets, movable shelters, and various implements of war, will take up to three whole months; and the piling up of mounds over against the walls will take three months more.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The general, unable to control his irritation, will launch his men to the assault like swarming ants, with the result that one-third of his men are slain, while the town still remains untaken. Such are the disastrous effects of a siege.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Therefore the skilful leader subdues the enemy’s troops without any fighting; he captures their cities without laying siege to them; he overthrows their kingdom without lengthy operations in the field.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: With his forces intact he will dispute the mastery of the Empire, and thus, without losing a man, his triumph will be complete. This is the method of attacking by stratagem.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: It is the rule in war, if our forces are ten to the enemy’s one, to surround him; if five to one, to attack him; if twice as numerous, to divide our army into two.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If equally matched, we can offer battle; if slightly inferior in numbers, we can avoid the enemy; quite unequal in every way, we can flee from him.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hence, though an obstinate fight may be made by a small force, in the end it must be captured by the larger force.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Now the general is the bulwark of the State; if the bulwark is complete at all points; the State will be strong; if the bulwark is defective, the State will be weak.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: There are three ways in which a ruler can bring misfortune upon his army:
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: By commanding the army to advance or to retreat, being ignorant of the fact that it cannot obey. This is called hobbling the army.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: By attempting to govern an army in the same way as he administers a kingdom, being ignorant of the conditions which are obtained in an army. This causes restlessness in the soldier’s minds.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Byemploying the officers of his army without discrimination, through ignorance of the military principle of adaptation to circumstances. This shakes the confidence of the soldiers.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Thus we may know that there are five essentials for victory:
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: He will win who knows when to fight and when not to fight.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: He will win if he knows how to handle both superior and inferior forces.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: He will win whose army is animated by the same spirit throughout all its ranks.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: He will win who, prepared himself, waits to take the enemy unprepared.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: He will win who has military capacity and is not interfered with by the sovereign.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: But when the army is restless and distrustful, trouble is sure to come from the other feudal princes. This is simply bringing anarchy into the army, and flinging victory away.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hence the saying: If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles. If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat. If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Tactical Dispositions
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Sun Tzu said: The good fighters of old first put themselves beyond the possibility of defeat, and then waited for an opportunity of defeating the enemy.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: To secure ourselves against defeat lies in our own hands, but the opportunity of defeating the enemy is provided by the enemy himself.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Thus the good fighter is able to secure himself against defeat, but cannot make certain of defeating the enemy.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hence the saying: One may know how to conquer without being able to do it.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Security against defeat implies defensive tactics; ability to defeat the enemy means taking the offensive.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Standing on the defensive indicates insufficient strength; attacking, a superabundance of strength.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The general who is skilled in defence hides in the most secret recesses of the earth; he who is skilled in attack flashes forth from the topmost heights of heaven. Thus on the one hand we have the ability to protect ourselves; on the other, a victory that is complete.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The general who is skilled in defence hides in the most secret recesses of the earth; he who is skilled in attack flashes forth from the topmost heights of heaven. Thus on the one hand we have the ability to protect ourselves; on the other, a victory that is complete.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: To see victory only when it is within the ken of the common herd is not the acme of excellence.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: To see victory only when it is within the ken of the common herd is not the acme of excellence.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Neither is it the acme of excellence if you fight and conquer and the whole Empire says, “Well done!”
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: To lift an autumn hair is no sign of great strength; to see the sun and moon is no sign of sharp sight; to hear the noise of thunder is no sign of a quick ear.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: What the ancients called a clever fighter is one who not only wins, but excels in winning with ease.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hence his victories bring him neither reputation for wisdom nor credit for courage.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: He wins his battles by making no mistakes. Making no mistakes is what establishes the certainty of victory, for it means conquering an enemy that is already defeated.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hence the skilful fighter puts himself into a position which makes defeat impossible, and does not miss the moment for defeating the enemy.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Thus it is that in war the victorious strategist only seeks battle after the victory has been won, whereas he who is destined to defeat first fights and afterwards looks for victory.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The consummate leader cultivates the moral law, and strictly adheres to method and discipline; thus it is in his power to control success.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: In respect of military methods, we have, firstly, Measurement; secondly, Estimation of quantity; thirdly, Calculation; fourthly, Balancing of chances; fifthly, Victory.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Measurement owes its existence to Earth; Estimation of quantity to Measurement; Calculation to Estimation of quantity; Balancing of chances to Calculation; and Victory to Balancing of chances.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: A victorious army opposed to a routed one, is as a pound’s weight placed in the scale against a single grain.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The onrush of a conquering force is like the bursting of pent-up waters into a chasm a thousand fathoms deep.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Energy
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Sun Tzu said: The control of a large force is the same principle as the control of a few men: it is merely a question of dividing up their numbers.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Fighting with a large army under your command is noisily different from fighting with a small one: it is merely a question of instituting signs and signals.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: To ensure that your whole host may withstand the brunt of the enemy’s attack and remain unshaken— this is affected by manoeuvres direct and indirect.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: That the impact of your army may be like a grindstone dashed against an egg—this is affected by the science of weak points and strong.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: In all fighting, the direct method may be used for joining battle, but indirect methods will be needed in order to secure victory.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Indirect tactics, efficienly applied, are inexhaustible as Heaven and Earth, unending as the flow of rivers and streams; like the sun and moon, they end but to begin anew; like the four seasons, they pass away to return once more.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: There are not more than five musical notes, yet the combinations of these five give rise to more melodies than can ever be heard.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: There are not more than five primary colours (blue, yellow, red, white, and black), yet in combination they produce more hours than can ever be seen.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: There are not more than five cardinal tastes (sour, acrid, salt, sweet, bitter), yet combinations of them yield more flavours than can ever be tasted.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: In battle, there are not more than two methods of attack—the direct and the indirect; yet these two in combination give rise to an endless series of manoeuvres.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The direct and the indirect lead on to each other in turn. It is like moving in a circle—you never come to an end. Who can exhaust the possibilities of their combination?
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The onset of troops is like the rush of a torrent which will even roll stones along in its course.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The quality of decision is like the well-timed swoop of a falcon which enables it to strike and destroy its victim.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Therefore the good fighter will be terrible in his onset, and prompt in his decision.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Energy may be likened to the bending of a crossbow; decision, to the releasing of a trigger.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Amid the turmoil and tumult of battle, there may be seeking disorder and yet no real disorder at all; amid confusion and chaos, your array may be without head or tail, yet it will be proof against defeat.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Simulated disorder postulates perfect discipline, simulated fear postulates courage; simulated weakness postulates strength.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hiding order beneath the cloak of disorder is simply a question of subdivision; concealing courage under a show of timidity presupposes a fund of latent energy; masking strength with weakness is to be affected by tactical dispositions.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Thus one who is skilful at keeping the enemy on the move maintains deceitful appearances, according to which the enemy will act. He sacrifices something, that the enemy may snatch at it.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: By holding out baits, he keeps him on the march; then with a body of picked men he lies in wait for him.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The clever combatant looks to the effect of combined energy, and does not require too much from individuals. Hence his ability to pick out the right men and utilize combined energy.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When he utilises combined energy, his fighting men become as it were like unto rolling logs or stones. For it is the nature of a log or stone to remain motionless on level ground, and to move when on a slope; if four-cornered, to come to a standstill, but if round-shaped, to go rolling down.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Thus the energy developed by good fighting men is as the momentum of a round stone rolled down a mountain thousands of feet in height. So much on the subject of energy.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Weak & Strong Points
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Sun Tzu said: Whoever is first in the field and awaits the coming of the enemy, will be fresh for the fight; whoever is second in the field and has to hasten to battle will arrive exhausted.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Therefore the clever combatant imposes his will on the enemy, but does not allow the enemy’s will to be imposed on him.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: By holding out advantages to him, he can cause the enemy to approach of his own accord; or, by inflicting damage, he can make it impossible for the enemy to draw near.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If the enemy is taking his ease, he can harass him; if well supplied with food, he can starve him out; if quietly encamped, he can force him to move.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Appear at points which the enemy must hasten to defend; march swiftly to places where you are not expected.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: An army may march great distances without distress, if it marches through a country where the enemy is not.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: You can be sure of succeeding in your attacks if you only attack places which are undefended. You can ensure the safety of your defence if you only hold positions that cannot be attacked.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Hence that general is skilful in attack whose opponent does not know what to defend; and he is skilful in defence whose opponent does not know what to attack.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: O divine art of subtlety and secrecy! Through you we learn to be invisible, through you inaudible; and hence we can hold the enemy’s fate in our hands.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: You may advance and be absolutely irresistible, if you make for the enemy’s weak points; you may retire and be safe from pursuit if your movements are more rapid than those of the enemy.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If we wish to fight, the enemy can be forced into an engagement even though he is sheltered behind a high rampart and a deep ditch. All we need to do is attack some other place that he will be obliged to relieve.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If we do not wish to fight, we can prevent the enemy from engaging us even though the lines of our encampment are merely traced out on the ground. All we need to do is to throw something odd and unaccountable in his way.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: By discovering the enemy’s dispositions and remaining invisible ourselves, we can keep our forces concentrated, while the enemy’s must be divided.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: We can form a single united body, while the enemy must split up into fractions. Hence there will be a whole pitted against separate parts of a whole, which means that we shall be many to the enemy’s few.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: And if we are able thus to attack an inferior force with a superior one, our opponents will be in dire straits.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Numerical weakness comes from having to prepare against possible attacks; numerical strength, from compelling our adversary to make these preparations against us.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: For should the enemy strengthen his van, he will weaken his rear; should he strengthen his rear, he will weaken his van; should he strengthen his left, he will weaken his right; should he strengthen his right, he will weaken his left. If he sends reinforcements everywhere, he will be weak everywhere.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The spot where we intend to fight must not be made known; for then the enemy will have to prepare against a possible attack at several different points; and his forces being thus distributed in many directions, the numbers we shall have to face at any given point will be proportionately few.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: But if neither time nor place be known, then the left wing will be impotent to succor the right, the right equally impotent to succor the left, the van unable to relieve the rear, or the rear to support the van. How much more so if the furthest portions of the army are anything under a hundred LI apart, and even the nearest are separated by several LI!
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Knowing the place and the time of the coming battle, we may concentrate from the greatest distances in order to fight.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Though according to my estimate the soldiers of Yueh exceed our own in number, that shall advantage them nothing in the matter of victory. I say then that victory can be achieved.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Though the enemy is stronger in numbers, we may prevent him from fighting. Scheme so as to discover his plans and the likelihood of their success.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Rouse him, and learn the principle of his activity or inactivity. Force him to reveal himself, so as to find out his vulnerable spots.

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: While we keep away from such places, we should get the enemy to approach them; while we face them, we should let the enemy have them on his rear.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If in the neighbourhood of your camp there should be any hilly country, ponds surrounded by aquatic grass, hollow basins filled with reeds, or woods with thick undergrowth, they must be carefully routed out and searched; for these are places where men in ambush or insidious spies are likely to be lurking.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If his place of encampment is easy to access, he is tendering a bait.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

When it branches out in different directions, it shows that parties have been sent to collect firewood. A few clouds of dust moving to and fro signify that the army is encamping.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When the light chariots come out first and take up a position on the wings, it is a sign that the enemy is forming for battle.

source_text_or_hash: Peace proposals unaccompanied by a sworn covenant indicate a plot.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When there is much running about and the soldiers fall into rank, it means that the critical moment has come.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When some are seen advancing and some retreating, it is a lure.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When the soldiers stand leaning on their spears, they are faint from want of food.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If those who are sent to draw water begin by drinking themselves, the army is suffering from thirst.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If the enemy sees an advantage to be gained and makes no effort to secure it, the soldiers are exhausted.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If birds gather on any spot, it is unoccupied. Clamour by night betokens nervousness.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If there is disturbance in the camp, the general’s authority is weak. If the banners and flags are shifted about, sedition is afoot. If the officers are angry, it means that the men are weary.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When an army feeds its horses with grain and kills its cattle for food, and when the men do not hang their cooking-pots over the camp-fires, showing that they will not return to their tents, you may know that they are determined to fight to the death.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The sight of men whispering together in small knots or speaking in subdued tones points to disaffection amongst the rank and file.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Too frequent rewards signify that the enemy is at the end of his resources; too many punishments betray a condition of dire distress.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: To begin by bluster, but afterwards to take fright at the enemy’s numbers, shows a supreme lack of intelligence.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When envoys are sent with compliments in their mouths, it is a sign that the enemy wishes for a truce.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If the enemy’s troops march up angrily and remain facing ours for a long time without either joining battle or taking themselves off again, the situation is one that demands great vigilance and circumspection.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: He who exercises no forethought but makes light of his opponents is sure to be captured by them.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Ground which can be abandoned but is hard to re-occupy is called entangling.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: With regard to ground of this nature, be before the enemy in occupying the raised and sunny spots, and carefully guard your line of supplies. Then you will be able to fight with advantage.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When the position is such that neither side will gain by making the first move, it is called temporising ground.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: In a position of this sort, even though the enemy should offer us an attractive bait, it will be advisable not to stir forth, but rather to retreat, thus enticing the enemy in his turn; then, when part of his army has come out, we may deliver our attack with advantage.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: With regard to narrow passes, if you can occupy them first, let them be strongly garrisoned and await the advent of the enemy.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Should the army forestall you in occupying a pass, do not go after him if the pass is fully garrisoned, but only if it is weakly garrisoned.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: With regard to precipitous heights, if you are beforehand with your adversary, you should occupy the raised and sunny spots, and wait for him to come up.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If the enemy has occupied them before you, do not follow him, but retreat and try to entice him away.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: When a general, unable to estimate the enemy’s strength, allows an inferior force to engage a larger one, or hurls a weak detachment against a powerful one, and neglects to place picked soldiers in the front rank, the result must be rout.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: These are six ways of courting defeat, which must be carefully noted by the general who has attained a responsible post.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: The general who advances without coveting fame and retreats without fearing disgrace, whose only thought is to protect his country and do good service for his sovereign, is the jewel of the kingdom.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Regard your soldiers as your children, and they will follow you into the deepest valleys; look upon them as your own beloved sons, and they will stand by you even unto death.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: If, however, you are indulgent, but unable to make your authority felt; kind-hearted, but unable to enforce your commands; and incapable, moreover, of quelling disorder: then your soldiers must be likened to spoiled children; they are useless for any practical purpose.
